newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa province says gaming bids may be amended.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa province says gaming bids may be amended.

text.p: The Gaming Board of South Africa's eastern Mpumulanga province said on Friday Tsogo Sun and Global Resorts, the preferred finalists for casino licences in the region, will be allowed to amend their applications.
The Board said in a statement there was an apparent need by the public for more detailed information on the nature and extent of the casino projects they had proposed.

It said it had allowed the amendments as it was convinced they were aimed at improving the quality of information and did not change the nature of the proposals on which the Board's selection was based nor the merits of its choice.
Legislation passed last year legalises casino gambling in South Africa for the first time and provinces have been given powers to issue licences under the National Gambling Act.
The Board said it had received 10 objections against the proposed casinos, stemming from church organisations, companies that were not selected as preferred finalists and an environmental body.
Tsogo is a joint-venture between a black consortium and South African Breweries Ltd's hotels unit, Southern Sun, as a preferred bidder to run gaming operations.
Global Resorts is a consortium consisting of Rand Merchant Bank, Genbel Securities Ltd and Malaysia's Mycom Berhad.
The Board said the amendments would cause a delay of two to three weeks in the process of finally granting licences. They were originally expected to be granted in March with casinos opening in July.
